questions.stem: The 'Quit India' movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on:
questions.explanation: On 8 August 1942, the AICC at Gowalia Tank Maidan (Mumbai) passed the Quit India Resolution; Gandhi gave the 'Karo ya Maro' (Do or Die) call. The next day, 9 August, top Congress leaders (Gandhi, Nehru, Patel, Azad) were arrested; the movement went underground with Jayaprakash Narayan, Aruna Asaf Ali (hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank), Ram Manohar Lohia, Usha Mehta (Congress Radio) leading it.

questions.stem: The Cripps Mission came to India in 1942 with an offer of:

options.option_text: Dominion status after the Second World War
Direct British rule for 30 more years

questions.explanation: Stafford Cripps (March-April 1942) offered Dominion Status after the war + the right of provinces / princely states to opt out of the Indian Union (a non-accession clause). Congress rejected the offer as a 'post-dated cheque on a failing bank' (attributed to Gandhi). The Muslim League also rejected it because it did not concede Pakistan outright. The failure of the Cripps Mission led directly to Quit India.

questions.stem: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 — which proposed a federation of three groups of provinces — had as one of its members:
questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission (1946) consisted of Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander. It proposed a three-tier federal union with three groupings of provinces and rejected Pakistan. Its plan was initially accepted by Congress and the Muslim League but quickly broke down. Mountbatten — Last Viceroy, 1947. Irwin — famous for the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931). Curzon — Viceroy 1899-1905, known for the Partition of Bengal 1905.

questions.stem: The Indian Independence Act 1947 was passed by the Parliament of:
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act — passed by the British Parliament on 18 July 1947 — legally created the two Dominions of India and Pakistan on 15 August 1947. Royal assent was given the same day. India was granted full legislative sovereignty on that date. Our own Constituent Assembly (elected 1946) began sitting from 9 December 1946 and completed drafting the Constitution on 26 November 1949 (adopted; brought into force on 26 January 1950).

questions.stem: Gandhi's famous 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro) call was given during which movement?
questions.explanation: 'Karo ya Maro' — delivered by Gandhi at Gowalia Tank Maidan, 8 August 1942. Non-Cooperation (1920-22) — 'Swaraj in one year'. Civil Disobedience (1930) — Dandi Salt March, 'I'll break the salt law'. Other big slogans — 'Inquilab Zindabad' (Bhagat Singh / Hasrat Mohani), 'Jai Hind' + 'Tum mujhe khoon do' (Bose), 'Swaraj is my birthright' (Tilak), 'Vande Mataram' (Bankim Chandra).

questions.stem: The last Viceroy of British India (and the first Governor-General of independent India from August 1947 to June 1948) was:
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten — the last Viceroy (arrived March 1947) and first GG of independent India (August 1947 to June 1948). C. Rajagopalachari succeeded him as the first (and only) Indian GG (June 1948 to January 1950), until the post was abolished with the Constitution. Lord Wavell preceded Mountbatten; Linlithgow oversaw WW-II years and the Quit India crackdown.

questions.stem: The Radcliffe Line that divided India and Pakistan in 1947 was drawn by:
questions.explanation: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired the Boundary Commission that drew the India-Pakistan border between July and August 1947 — despite having never visited India before. He had just five weeks. The line divided Punjab and Bengal, triggered the partition massacres and one of the largest human migrations in history (est. 14-18 million displaced). The line was made public on 17 August 1947 — two days AFTER independence.
